Re: Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Emerson Kimura
Member ID: W623723443
Reference Number: POC-0B7F2515DA-96515
Date of Notice: 2026-08-03
Requested Service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Treating Surgeon: Dr. Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery
Appeal Deadline Stated on Notice: 2027-01-30

To the Appeals Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), as communicated in your Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03. The notice states that the request was denied because "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," and that the determination "was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." The notice does not name or cite that medical policy, provide its policy number, or attach a copy of the clinical review criteria that were applied to my case.

1. The specific criteria relied upon have not been identified or provided to me.

I attempted to locate a Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative / CareSource medical policy specific to hip arthroscopy, femoroacetabular impingement (FAI), or hip preservation surgery, using the plan's own published current and archived Wisconsin Marketplace medical policy libraries. I was unable to find any such document; the published lists do not include any policy addressing this procedure or CPT code. Because I have not been able to obtain or review the actual criteria used to deny my request, I am not able to fully respond point-by-point to whatever specific thresholds were applied. I am not quoting or asserting any specific plan policy language here because none has been produced to me.

I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that CareSource/Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative provide me with a copy of the specific medical policy, clinical guideline, or review criteria that was applied to deny CPT 29914 in my case, free of charge, so that I and my surgeon can respond directly to it. If no such written, procedure-specific policy exists and the determination was instead based on a general reviewer judgment or a licensed third-party guideline (e.g., an internal clinical review tool), I ask that this be disclosed as well, including the name of that guideline and the specific criteria within it that were found not to be met.

2. Without a cited policy to respond to, the clinical facts below demonstrate that this procedure is medically necessary under the generally accepted, evidence-based indications for hip arthroscopy in the setting of symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement with labral tear.

- Symptom duration and severity: I have had 12 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and I am currently unable to run or squat.

- Failed conservative treatment: I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-04-30 through 2026-06-25, 16 visits) focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of symptoms. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-27 that provided only two weeks of partial relief. This represents a substantial, well-documented trial of nonoperative management that has failed.

- Objective imaging confirmation: MRI arthrogram of the hip performed 2026-06-26 demonstrates an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, an alpha angle of 68 degrees, preserved joint space, and Tönnis grade 0 (i.e., no significant osteoarthritis). This is the classic imaging profile associated with a favorable outcome from arthroscopic treatment of FAI and labral pathology.

- Physical examination findings: Positive provocative impingement testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion corroborate the imaging findings and the reported functional limitations.

- No contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker, so there are no medical contraindications to surgery.

Taken together — 12 months of unremitting symptoms, a completed and documented course of supervised physical therapy, 8 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection all without durable relief, combined with MRI-confirmed labral tear and cam FAI with a preserved joint space (Tönnis 0) — this presentation reflects the type of case in which hip arthroscopy is considered medically necessary treatment by the orthopedic community when conservative care has been exhausted and advanced arthritis is absent. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, can provide a supporting letter of medical necessity addressing these same points in further clinical detail if that would assist your review; please advise if this has not already been included in the file.

3. Requested action.

I ask that CareSource/Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative:
(a) reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29914 as medically necessary; or, in the alternative,
(b) provide the specific medical policy or clinical guideline used to deny this request, including its title, number, and effective date, so that I may supplement this appeal with a further point-by-point response within any remaining time before the appeal deadline of 2027-01-30 or any applicable extension.

I understand that CareSource is required to acknowledge receipt of this appeal and to issue a decision within the standard internal appeal timeframe. If this appeal is denied, I intend to exercise my right to an independent external review (through MAXIMUS Federal Services or the federal external review process at https://externalappeal.cms.gov, as applicable) and I request that the denial letter clearly explain how to initiate that external review.

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-30 to 2026-06-25)
- Medication history documenting 8 months of NSAID use and the 2026-03-27 corticosteroid injection
- MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-26
- Relevant imaging (if available)
- Office/exam notes documenting positive provocative testing and functional limitations
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes, if separately submitted]
- [Appointment of Representative form, if this appeal is being submitted by someone acting on my behalf]

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email above. I can be reached at [phone number] with any questions.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Emerson Kimura
